hello.note: Polite, for anyone, at any time; also goodbye. Friends say Γεια σου (YA soo)

how-are-you.note: Polite and the same for anyone. The Greek question mark looks like a semicolon: ;

good-morning.note: Until early afternoon. Then Καλησπέρα (ka-lee-SPE-ra), good evening

goodbye.note: Γεια σας, hello, is just as common for goodbye

please.note: Also means you're welcome and can I help you?

thank-you.note: Ευχαριστώ πολύ (po-LEE) means thank you very much

yes.note: Careful: ne means yes. Greeks may also nod down for yes and tilt the head up, with a click of the tongue, for no

excuse-me.note: Sorry, and excuse me to get attention or get past

my-name.note: Literally "they call me". The audio uses Peter as the example name

your-name.note: Polite and the same for anyone

dont-understand.note: The same for a man or a woman

speak-english.note: Most people in tourist areas do

would-like.note: Literally "I would like", the same for a man or a woman. The audio uses έναν καφέ (E-nan ka-FE), a coffee

i-want.note: More direct. The audio uses αυτό (af-TO), this one

discount.note: Literally "will you give me a discount?" Fine at markets and small shops, especially when buying several things

card.note: Cards are widely taken; small tavernas and kiosks may prefer cash

bill.note: Waiters won't bring the bill until you ask. Often a free dessert or shot comes with it

wifi.text: Ποιος είναι ο κωδικός για το Wi-Fi;
wifi.say: pyos EE-ne o ko-dhee-KOS ya to WAI-fai

toilet.note: Πού (poo) means where. Put toilet paper in the bin, not the toilet: the pipes are narrow

taxi.text: Μπορείτε να μου καλέσετε ένα ταξί;
taxi.say: bo-REE-te na moo ka-LE-se-te E-na ta-KSEE
taxi.note: Apps such as FreeNow and Uber call regular taxis

bus.note: Long-distance and island buses are run by KTEL (k-TEL). Islands are reached by ferry, πλοίο (PLEE-o)

which-train.note: Literally "which train goes to the...?" The audio uses Θεσσαλονίκη (the-sa-lo-NEE-kee), Thessaloniki

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Thessaloniki as the example

trip-length.note: The audio uses Thessaloniki as the example
trip-length.spoken: Πόση ώρα κάνει μέχρι τη Θεσσαλονίκη;

allergic.note: Literally "I have an allergy to", the same for a man or a woman. With the: στους ξηρούς καρπούς (stoos ksee-ROOS kar-POOS) nuts, στα θαλασσινά (sta tha-la-see-NA) seafood, στα αυγά (sta av-GHA) eggs. The audio uses nuts

love-dish.text: Μου αρέσει πολύ αυτό το φαγητό!
love-dish.say: moo a-RE-see po-LEE af-TO to fa-yee-TO
love-dish.note: Literally "I like this food a lot"

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

recommend.note: Dishes are often shared: order a few mezédes for the table

beer.note: Mythos and Fix are Greek beers. Ouzo is drunk with food, diluted with water

coffee.note: Cold coffees, freddo espresso and frappé, are the summer favourites. Say how sweet: σκέτο (SKE-to) none, μέτριο (ME-tryo) medium, γλυκό (ghlee-KO) sweet

water.note: Tap water is safe in most of Greece; on some islands, drink bottled

hot.note: Hot, of food and drinks, and the weather

help.note: Shout it. For any emergency, call 112

need-doctor.note: The same for a man or a woman. For an ambulance, call 166 or 112

pharmacy.note: Look for the green cross. Pharmacists give good advice for small problems
